# ReqQuest UI: components and authoring guide

Everything needed to write UI in a ReqQuest project, in one file. Read the section you need; you are
not meant to read it end to end.

Versions this describes (the versions a downstream project resolves through `@reqquest/ui`):

| package | version |
|---|---|
| `@reqquest/ui` | 1.12.1 |
| `@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte` | 1.11.0 |
| `@txstate-mws/svelte-forms` | 2.1.9 |
| `carbon-components-svelte` | 0.110.2 |
| `carbon-icons-svelte` | 13.15.0 |
| `svelte` | 5.x, **no runes** |

## Rules that apply to every file

The component preference ladder, in order. Go down a rung only when the rung above genuinely has
nothing:

1. **`@reqquest/ui`** - the ReqQuest layer. `QuestionnairePrompt`, `PromptDisplayGrid`/`PromptDisplayRow`,
   `InfoCard`, `CommentCard`, `FieldCardRadio`, `FieldCardCheckbox`.
2. **`@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte`** - the house component library. `ColumnList` over Carbon's
   `DataTable` in almost every situation.
3. **`carbon-components-svelte`** - raw Carbon, when nothing above fits.
4. **Raw HTML/CSS** - last resort, and reuse Carbon's CSS classes and `--cds-*` custom properties
   rather than inventing colors.

Everything else:

- **Svelte 5, but no runes.** `export let`, `$:`, `<slot>`, `$$slots`, `<svelte:fragment>`,
  `on:click`. The whole codebase is Svelte 4 syntax on the Svelte 5 compiler; do not mix in `$state`
  or `$props`.
- **SPA, no SSR.** SvelteKit with `adapter-static`. Nothing runs on a server; there is no
  `+page.server.ts`.
- **Icons** come from `carbon-icons-svelte`, deep-imported one per line -
  `import Launch from 'carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Launch.svelte'`. Never the package barrel; it pulls
  thousands of components into the bundle.
- **Dates** use luxon.
- **Member order** in a `.svelte` file: `<script>`, then markup, then `<style>`.
- **ESLint** is `eslint-config-love` plus `@stylistic`: 2-space indent, single quotes, no trailing
  comma, space before a function's paren, `arrow-parens: as-needed`.
- **Tailwind** is available and widely used in existing prompt components, but the framework's
  standing preference is to avoid it - it may be deprecated. Do not add new utility soup, and do not
  strip it out of files that already have it. One hard constraint if you do use it: the
  `@tailwindcss/container-queries` plugin is **not installed**, so `@[48rem]:` utilities compile to
  nothing and fail silently. Write a real `@container` rule against an element with
  `[container-type:inline-size]` instead.
- **Colors** come from Carbon custom properties (`--cds-text-02`, `--cds-border-subtle`,
  `--cds-support-03`, `--cds-link-primary`), never hex literals, so theming holds.
- **Toasts** come from `toasts.add()` in `@txstate-mws/svelte-components`.

## What "building UI" means in a ReqQuest project

A downstream ReqQuest project owns exactly one directory: **`ui/src/local`**. Routes, the `UIShell`,
the reviewer and applicant screens, and the GraphQL client all come from the framework - either from
`node_modules/@reqquest/ui` (what your editor and `svelte-check` see) or, in the production image,
from the GitHub source tarball the `ui/Dockerfile` untars at the tag pinned in
`package.json` → `reqquest.ui_base_tag`, which then does `rm -rf src/local` and copies yours in.

So a new screen is almost never a route. It is a **prompt**: one API-side definition supplying the
key, and one or two Svelte components on the UI side supplying the pixels.

### The prompt pair

Each prompt is a pair of colocated components, grouped in a folder per phase or program
(`prequal/`, `hazlewood/`, `reviewer/`):

```
ui/src/local/prequal/BenefitSituation.svelte         formComponent  - collects the answer
ui/src/local/prequal/BenefitSituationDisplay.svelte  displayComponent - renders it read-only
```

`displayComponent` is required; `formComponent` is optional, and leaving it out declares the prompt
as automation-filled. Both are registered together under the prompt's key.

### The props the framework hands your component

Both members of the pair are mounted with `<svelte:component>`, so they are untyped
(`Component<any>`) - declare with `export let` and only the ones you use.

| prop | form | display | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | yes | yes | the prompt's own answer object. In a form it is the live svelte-forms state; in a display it is the saved answer. |
| `appRequestData` | yes | yes | every prompt's data on this app request, keyed by prompt key. |
| `prestageData` | yes | yes | `{ latest, current }` - data staged by an automation before the prompt was shown. |
| `fetched` | yes | - | whatever the API definition's `fetch` returned; where dynamic option lists arrive. |
| `configData` | yes | yes | this prompt's own period configuration. |
| `gatheredConfigData` | yes | yes | configuration gathered from related definitions. |
| `invalidated` / `invalidatedReason` | yes | yes | set when a reviewer sent the prompt back for correction. |
| `appRequestId` | **sometimes** | yes | present on the applicant page, the opt-out modal, the display path, and the `formMode: 'full'` modal - but **not** on the reviewer's inline edit form. Guard it, or register `formMode: 'full'` if you truly need it. |

`prestageData` has a trap worth knowing before you hit it. Read the **prop**, not the mutation:

```svelte
$: prestage = prestageData.latest ?? prestageData.current
$: if (data) data.__prestage = prestage   // still set it, so it gets submitted
```

Deriving your view from `data.__prestage` instead looks equivalent and is not: a property mutation
(rather than a reassignment) loses Svelte's cross-block invalidation on an SPA transition, and the
component renders empty until a hard refresh.

## Registering a prompt

Registration lives in `ui/src/local/index.ts`. Two things there are load-bearing and easy to get
wrong.

**Annotate the config literal, then construct the registry.** `UIRegistry`'s constructor takes a
widened `AnyUIConfig`, so `new UIRegistry({ ... })` inline type-checks *nothing*:

```ts
const config: UIConfig = {        // exhaustiveness is enforced HERE, by the annotation
  /* ... */
}
export const uiRegistry = new UIRegistry(config)
```

**Use the keyed-object form, never an array.** `prompts` is a total mapped type over the generated
`PromptKey` union, so a prompt the API defines and the UI forgot is a *build error*. An array can
only reject keys that do not exist; it can never require the ones that do, and it resolves duplicates
last-wins in silence. `requirements` and `programs` are partial by design - they carry only optional
decoration (an icon, a configure component) and every consumer optional-chains them - but they still
reject unknown keys.

Keys must be **literal**, one per line. A computed key cannot satisfy `PromptKey`, so a loop over a
program list defeats the whole mechanism even though it compiles.

```ts
import { UIRegistry, type UIConfig, type PromptDefinition, type PromptKey } from '@reqquest/ui'
import { GeneralTextSkeleton } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
import BenefitSituation from './prequal/BenefitSituation.svelte'
import BenefitSituationDisplay from './prequal/BenefitSituationDisplay.svelte'

// Prompt skeletons are opt-in per prompt since reqquest 1.8.0. Without a `loader` the applicant
// apply route and the reviewer edit dialog render an empty area while the prompt's data is in
// flight. Every prompt here waits on a round-trip, so default them all; the delay keeps the
// skeleton from flashing on a fast or cached load.
const DEFAULT_PROMPT_LOADER = { skeletonComponent: GeneralTextSkeleton, delay: 200 }
type PromptRegistrations = Record<PromptKey, Omit<PromptDefinition, 'key'>>
function withDefaultLoader (prompts: PromptRegistrations): PromptRegistrations {
  for (const prompt of Object.values(prompts)) prompt.loader ??= DEFAULT_PROMPT_LOADER
  return prompts
}

const config: UIConfig = {
  appName: 'Veteran Affairs Certification Request',
  terminology: { appRequest: 'Request', login: 'Net ID', period: 'Term' },
  programs: { chapter_33: {}, hazlewood_veteran: {} },
  requirements: { eligibility_questions_prequal_req: {} },
  prompts: withDefaultLoader({
    benefit_situation_prompt: {
      formComponent: BenefitSituation,
      displayComponent: BenefitSituationDisplay
    },
    reviewer_course_info_cert_prompt: {
      formComponent: CourseInfo,
      displayComponent: CourseInfoDisplay,
      formMode: 'full'
    }
  })
}
export const uiRegistry = new UIRegistry(config)
```

### `PromptDefinition`

- **`displayComponent`** `Component` **(required)** - read-only rendering. Keep it compact; it appears
  in a long list of prompts.
- **`formComponent`** `Component` - the data-collection screen. Omit only for an automation-filled
  prompt; the applicant view cannot handle a prompt with no form, so applicant-facing prompts always
  need one.
- **`formMode`** `'small' | 'large' | 'full'` (default `'small'`) - the area the form is rendered in.
  `'small'` is about 8 lines at 320px; `'large'` about 32 lines at 800px; `'full'` is a full-screen
  modal, which also **disables autosave in the reviewer UI** and is what supplies `appRequestId` to
  the reviewer form. All three must stay responsive down to 320px.
- **`displayMode`** `'small' | 'large'` (default `'small'`) - there is deliberately no `'full'`,
  because the whole prompt list has to print on one page. Use `'large'` together with
  `PromptDisplayGrid` when one prompt collects several question/answer pairs.
- **`automation`** `boolean` - marks the prompt as automation-filled, visually distinct. Defaults to
  true when there is no `formComponent`, and makes `formMode` behave like `'full'`. If you set it
  *and* supply a form, consider a hidden field marking the data as human-written so automations stop
  overwriting it.
- **`configureComponent`** / **`configureDisplayComponent`** `Component` - per-period configuration
  form and its read-only twin, always rendered in a full-screen modal. They receive `data` and
  `fetched` only.
- **`icon`** `Component` - navigation icon.
- **`loader`** `{ skeletonComponent, delay? } | boolean` (default `false`) - see the snippet above.
- **`applicantPromptPage`** `{ formClass?, invalidatedInlineNotificationClass? }` - per-prompt
  override of the CSS applied to the framework `Form` that wraps applicant prompts. The global
  version of the same setting lives on `UIConfig`.

### Keys, and how they stay honest

`PromptKey`, `RequirementKey` and `ProgramKey` come from a generated declaration that augments
`@reqquest/ui`:

```ts
// ui/src/local/keys.generated.d.ts - GENERATED, commit it
export {}
declare module '@reqquest/ui' {
  interface ReqQuestKeys {
    prompts: 'benefit_situation_prompt' | 'veteran_ssn_prompt'
    requirements: 'eligibility_questions_prequal_req'
    programs: 'chapter_33'
  }
}
```

Three ways this silently does nothing, all of which look fine in an editor:

- **The `export {}` is load-bearing.** Without a top-level import or export the file is a global
  script and `declare module` *replaces* `@reqquest/ui` instead of augmenting it - every import from
  the package then fails with "has no exported member".
- **It must fall inside your tsconfig `include`**, or it augments nothing and every key type quietly
  degrades to `string`.
- **It goes stale.** Regenerate from the API project after adding, removing, renaming or re-keying a
  definition, and gate it in CI:

  ```
  node node_modules/@reqquest/api/dist/analysis/cli.js <api-project> \
    --emit-keys ../ui/src/local/keys.generated.d.ts --module '@reqquest/ui'
  node node_modules/@reqquest/api/dist/analysis/cli.js <api-project> \
    --check-keys ../ui/src/local/keys.generated.d.ts --module '@reqquest/ui'
  ```

  The generator builds a real TypeScript program over the API's `.ts` sources, so it is an
  API-repo tool. A UI repo that only consumes a published `@reqquest/api` can receive a declaration
  but cannot produce one. See `docs/downstream-setup.md` in the reqquest repo for the full procedure.

Nothing in the framework runs your type check for you. Add one line to your build - `svelte-check`
narrowed to `src/local/index.ts` is enough, and is what the framework itself does in
`ui/check-registry.js`. Without it, the only remaining net is runtime: `UIRegistry.warnIfMissing`
logs an ungated `console.error` naming the key, and `MissingDefinitionNotification` renders in place
of the missing component. That is degradation, not detection.

## Recipes

Each of these is a complete file. Adapt, do not extend into something clever.

### 1. Minimal applicant prompt

No intro text, one question. The framework already wraps you in a `Form`, so there is no `Form`,
no submit button, and no `validate`/`submit` here - the API definition owns validation.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { FieldRadioTile } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
  export let fetched
  $: options = fetched.options ?? []
</script>

<div class="max-w-[550px] mx-auto mt-6">
  <FieldRadioTile
    required
    path="situation"
    items={options}
    orientation="horizontal"
    centerHorizontal
    descriptionVisibility="persistent"
  />
</div>
```

### 2. Applicant prompt with intro content and a conditional branch

`QuestionnairePrompt` supplies the `intro` slot, the external-links row, and the 800px centered
column. Note it has **no** `title` or `description` prop - the screen title comes from the API
definition. Put explanatory copy in the `intro` slot.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { QuestionnairePrompt } from '@reqquest/ui'
  import { ColumnList, FieldRadioTile, type ColumnDefinition } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
  import { InlineNotification } from 'carbon-components-svelte'
  export let data
  export let prestageData

  $: prestage = prestageData.latest ?? prestageData.current
  $: if (data) data.__prestage = prestage
  $: courses = (prestage?.nodes?.client?.data?.courses ?? []) as Course[]

  // AJV can hand a FieldRadioTile boolean back as the string 'true'/'false'. Coerce before testing.
  $: scheduleWrong = data.scheduleCorrect === false || data.scheduleCorrect === 'false'

  // ColumnList rows must carry an `id` - ColumnDefinition<T> constrains T to { id: string | number }
  // and uses it to key the rows. A row type without one will not type-check.
  interface Course { id: string, subject: string, courseNumber: string, title: string }
  const columns: ColumnDefinition<Course>[] = [
    { id: 'subject', label: 'Subject', get: 'subject' },
    { id: 'courseNumber', label: 'Course', get: 'courseNumber' },
    { id: 'title', label: 'Title', get: 'title' }
  ]
  const yesNo = [{ value: true, label: 'Yes' }, { value: false, label: 'No' }]
</script>

<QuestionnairePrompt externalLinks={[{ url: 'https://registrar.example.edu', label: 'Registrar' }]}>
  <div slot="intro">
    <p>Confirm the schedule below matches what you are enrolled in this term.</p>
    <ColumnList {columns} rows={courses} title="Final schedule" />
    <FieldRadioTile
      boolean
      required
      path="scheduleCorrect"
      items={yesNo}
      orientation="horizontal"
      centerHorizontal
      descriptionVisibility="persistent"
    />
  </div>
  <div class:hidden={!scheduleWrong}>
    <InlineNotification
      kind="warning"
      title="Schedule not final."
      subtitle="Finish registration before continuing."
      lowContrast
      hideCloseButton
    />
  </div>
</QuestionnairePrompt>
```

### 3. Display component, aligned with the prompt list

When a prompt collects several question/answer pairs that should each read as its own row on the
review screens, make `PromptDisplayGrid` the **root element** of the display component and register
the prompt with `displayMode: 'large'`. The surrounding screens hand it their column tracks via CSS
subgrid, so its rows are indistinguishable from real prompt rows and wrap at the same breakpoints.
Root element matters - wrap it in a `<div>` and the subgrid handoff silently stops working.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { PromptDisplayGrid, PromptDisplayRow } from '@reqquest/ui'
  export let data
  const word = (v: unknown) => v == null ? '' : v ? 'Yes' : 'No'
</script>

<PromptDisplayGrid>
  <PromptDisplayRow challenge="Can provide SSN documentation?">{word(data.canProvide)}</PromptDisplayRow>
  <PromptDisplayRow challenge="Document type" indentLevel={1}>{data.docType ?? ''}</PromptDisplayRow>
  <PromptDisplayRow full>
    <em>Uploaded {data.files?.length ?? 0} document(s).</em>
  </PromptDisplayRow>
</PromptDisplayGrid>
```

For a single-value prompt, `displayMode: 'small'` and a plain paragraph is fine and correct - do not
reach for the grid to display one answer.

### 4. Reviewer prompt in a full-screen modal

`formMode: 'full'` gives you the whole screen and supplies `appRequestId`. Lay out reference material
and questions yourself.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { FieldRadio, FieldTextArea } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
  import DocumentPreview from '../DocumentPreview.svelte'
  export let data
  export let appRequestId: string

  const yesNo = [{ value: true, label: 'Yes' }, { value: false, label: 'No' }]
  $: valid = data.documentValid === true || data.documentValid === 'true'
</script>

<div class="reviewer-layout">
  <section class="document">
    <!-- Reference material for the reviewer. `appRequestId` is what a document preview or an extra
         API call keys on, and it is the reason this prompt is registered `formMode: 'full'`. -->
    <DocumentPreview {appRequestId} promptKey="reviewer_document_prompt" fileProp="files" />
  </section>
  <section class="questions">
    <FieldRadio
      boolean
      required
      path="documentValid"
      legendText="Is the uploaded document valid?"
      items={yesNo}
      orientation="horizontal"
    />
    <!-- Hidden with CSS, not {#if}: the field must stay mounted so `conditional` can clear its
         value when the branch goes away. An {#if} unmounts it and the stale answer is submitted. -->
    <div class:hidden={valid}>
      <FieldTextArea
        path="rejectionReason"
        conditional={!valid}
        labelText="Why is it not valid?"
      />
    </div>
  </section>
</div>

<style>
  /* The container-queries Tailwind plugin is not installed, so `@[48rem]:` would be dead. */
  .reviewer-layout { container-type: inline-size; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1.5rem; }
  @container (min-width: 48rem) {
    .reviewer-layout { flex-direction: row; }
    .document, .questions { flex: 1; }
  }
</style>
```

### 5. Configuration component

Registered as `configureComponent` on a prompt or requirement. It receives `data` and `fetched`
only, and is always rendered in a full-screen modal.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { FieldNumber, FieldSelect } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
  export let fetched
  $: terms = fetched?.terms ?? []
</script>

<FieldNumber path="minimumCreditHours" labelText="Minimum credit hours" />
<FieldSelect path="term" labelText="Term" items={terms} />
```

## Field idioms

Three patterns that are not obvious from the prop tables and cause real bugs when missed.

**Coerce booleans.** AJV can return a `FieldRadio`/`FieldRadioTile` boolean as the string `'true'` or
`'false'`. `{#if data.flag}` is then true for `'false'`. Always narrow:

```svelte
$: yes = data.flag === true || data.flag === 'true'
$: no  = data.flag === false || data.flag === 'false'
```

**`conditional` clears stale data.** A field with `conditional={false}` is dropped from the submitted
data. Set it from the same expression that decides whether the branch is relevant, so an answer the
applicant gave and then navigated away from does not survive.

**Hide with CSS, never `{#if}`.** A field inside a removed `{#if}` block is unmounted, and an
unmounted field cannot clear its own value - the stale answer is submitted. Toggle `class:hidden`
(or a `visible` prop on a wrapper) so the field stays mounted and `conditional` does its job.

## ReqQuest components

Exported from `@reqquest/ui`. Prefer these over hand-rolled markup inside a prompt component.

### CommentCard

Import: `import { CommentCard } from '@reqquest/ui'`

#### Props

- **`content`** `string` **(required)** - The TEXT content of the comment.
- **`authorName`** `string` **(required)** - The full name of the author.
- **`authorLogin`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - The login name of the author (e.g. netid). Optional.
- **`createdAt`** `DateTime | string` **(required)** - The timestamp this comment was created. Accepts a Luxon DateTime or an ISO string.
- **`actions`** `ActionItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Actions available on this comment (shown as an overflow menu in the top right).
- **`noborder`** (default: `false`) - If true, the comment box will not have a background, drop shadow, or padding. Use this when rendering a comment in a context that already provides its own framing.

### FieldCardCheckbox

> A form field component that displays a grid of selectable cards (multiple selection). Similar to FieldCardRadio but allows selecting multiple cards (checkbox behavior). The form value is an array of selected item values. By default this component expects values to be strings. If you wish to use other types of values, you must provide a `serialize` and `deserialize` function that handle individual item values. If your `items` are not ready on first load (e.g. they're being loaded from an API fetch), you must place this field inside an `{#if}` block until they are ready.

Import: `import { FieldCardCheckbox } from '@reqquest/ui'`

#### Props

- **`path`** `string` **(required)** - Path to the form field in the data structure
- **`items`** `CardSelectItem[]` **(required)** - Array of card options
- **`conditional`** (default: `true`) - Whether the field group is conditional @default true
- **`notNull`** (default: `false`) - Set to true to prevent null/undefined values (will default to empty array) @default false
- **`defaultValue`** `any[]` (default: `[]`) - Default selected values (array) @default []
- **`legendText`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Text to display in the fieldset legend @default undefined
- **`required`** (default: `false`) - When true, the field is marked as required in the UI. This is only for visual indication and does not affect validation. Validation is handled by the API that receives the data. @default false
- **`cardSize`** (default: `'20rem'`) - CSS size for the grid minimum item width (like CardGrid) @default '20rem'
- **`gap`** (default: `'16px'`) - Gap between cards in the grid @default '16px'
- **`serialize`** `((value: any) => string) | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Custom function to serialize individual item values for form submission. Each item value is serialized independently before being stored in the array. @default undefined
- **`deserialize`** `((value: string) => any) | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Custom function to deserialize individual item values from form data. Each item value is deserialized independently after being retrieved from the array. @default undefined

### FieldCardRadio

> A form field component that displays a grid of selectable cards (single selection). Similar to FieldRadioTile but with richer card-based visuals including images and tags. By default this component expects values to be strings. If you wish to use other types of values, you must provide a `serialize` and `deserialize` function. If you set the `number` prop, an appropriate serializer and deserializer will be provided by default. If your `items` are not ready on first load (e.g. they're being loaded from an API fetch), you must place this field inside an `{#if}` block until they are ready.

Import: `import { FieldCardRadio } from '@reqquest/ui'`

#### Props

- **`path`** `string` **(required)** - Path to the form field in the data structure
- **`items`** `CardSelectItem[]` **(required)** - Array of card options
- **`number`** (default: `false`) - Set to true to treat the value as a number instead of string @default false
- **`boolean`** (default: `false`) - Set to true to treat the value as a boolean @default false
- **`notNull`** (default: `false`) - Set to true to prevent null values @default false
- **`conditional`** (default: `true`) - Whether the field group is conditional @default true
- **`defaultValue`** `any` (default: `undefined`) - Default selected value @default undefined
- **`legendText`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Text to display in the fieldset legend @default undefined
- **`required`** (default: `false`) - When true, the field is marked as required in the UI. This is only for visual indication and does not affect validation. Validation is handled by the API that receives the data. @default false
- **`cardSize`** (default: `'20rem'`) - CSS size for the grid minimum item width (like CardGrid) @default '20rem'
- **`gap`** (default: `'16px'`) - Gap between cards in the grid @default '16px'
- **`serialize`** `((value: any) => string) | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Custom function to serialize values for form submission @default undefined
- **`deserialize`** `((value: string) => any) | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Custom function to deserialize values from form data @default undefined

### InfoCard

Import: `import { InfoCard } from '@reqquest/ui'`

#### Props

- **`title`** `string` **(required)** - The title of the component.
- **`subhead`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - The subheading for the component, which is optional.
- **`emphasizeTitle`** (default: `false`) - Adds visual emphasis to the title
- **`actions`** `ActionItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Combined actions and navigations rendered as buttons at the bottom of the card.
- **`noPrimaryAction`** (default: `false`) - Prevents the first button from having primary styling.
- **`tags`** `TagItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Array of tag items to display on the card.
- **`tagsInBody`** (default: `false`) - Determines whether the tags should be displayed in the body of the card.
- **`role`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - The ARIA role for the card. Defaults to 'listitem' when nested inside a CardGrid, 'region' otherwise.

### PromptDisplayGrid

> Lays out a prompt's display data as challenge/response rows that align with the surrounding prompt list, for prompts that collect several question/answer pairs in a single form but should read as individual rows on the review screens. Rows take on the same padding and border treatment as the prompt rows around them, so each challenge/response is indistinguishable from a standalone prompt. Place this as the root element of a `displayComponent` and register the prompt with `displayMode: 'large'`. The full-width answer area becomes a subgrid of the prompt list, so rows share the exact column tracks of the real prompt rows around them and wrap at the same breakpoints. Fill it with `PromptDisplayRow` children; pass `full` on a row to span the entire width. It may also be the root element of a `formComponent` registered with `formMode: 'large'`: the reviewer screen's inline edit form is bridged into the same subgrid, so rows of field inputs align with the prompt rows too. Rendered anywhere without a prompt list around it (the edit modal, applicant pages), the grid falls back to laying out its own two columns.

Import: `import { PromptDisplayGrid } from '@reqquest/ui'`

<!-- no upstream doc at this version; props extracted from the component source -->

### PromptDisplayRow

> One challenge/response row inside a `PromptDisplayGrid`. The challenge lands in the same column as the prompt titles around it and the response in the answer column. - `challenge` prop or slot for the question, default slot for the answer. - `full` spans the entire grid width instead, for content that needs the whole row (documents, notes, notifications). - `indentLevel` indents the challenge (or full-row content) to suggest hierarchy, e.g. follow-up questions under a parent question.

Import: `import { PromptDisplayRow } from '@reqquest/ui'`

#### Props

- **`challenge`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - The question being answered. Use the `challenge` slot instead if you need markup.
- **`full`** (default: `false`) - Span the full width of the grid instead of splitting into challenge/response.
- **`indentLevel`** (default: `0`) - Indent the challenge (or full-row content) by this multiple of a small indent unit (1rem per level, tunable with --prompt-display-indent-size). Default 0.

## carbon-svelte: custom components

Imported from `@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte`.

### ActionSet

> A set of buttons typically used at the top of a Card, Panel, or ColumnList. This component provides consistent action button handling across multiple components.

Import: `import { ActionSet } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`
Types: `import type { ActionItem } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`actions`** `ActionItem[]` **(required)** - Array of Action Item's included in the set.
- **`noPrimaryAction`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Prevent first action from having primary button styling
- **`forceOverflow`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Force all actions into overflow menu
- **`maxButtons`** `number` (default: `2`) - Maximum number of buttons to show before using overflow menu
- **`light`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Use light theme variant
- **`includeLabels`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Show text labels alongside icons
- **`small`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Use small button size variant
- **`large`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Use large button size variant
- **`describedById`** `string` (default: empty string) - ID of element that describes these actions
- **`menuAlign`** `'auto' | 'topright' | 'bottomright' | 'bottomleft' | 'topleft'` (default: `'bottomright'`) - Alignment of the overflow menu compared to the overflow button 'auto' will align based on placement of the button in the viewport 'topright' will align the menu above the button with the right edges lined up 'bottomright' will align the menu below the button with the right edges lined up 'bottomleft' will align the menu below the button with the left edges lined up 'topleft' will align the menu above the button with the left edges lined up
- **`reverse`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Set this to true to reverse the order of the buttons and put the overflow menu on the right

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `ArrowLeft or ArrowDown` | Moves focus to next action |
| `ArrowRight or ArrowUp` | Moves focus to previous action |
| `Esc` | Closes the overflow menu if open |

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { ActionSet } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
  import { Edit, TrashCan, User } from 'carbon-icons-svelte'
</script>

<ActionSet actions={[
  {
    label: 'Edit',
    icon: Edit,
    href: 'https://www.txst.edu/'
  }, {
    label: 'Delete',
    icon: TrashCan,
    disabled: true
  }, {
    label: 'Manage Users',
    icon: User,
    onClick: () => { alert('Manage Users') }
  }
]} />
```

### Card

> A versatile container component that organizes content with a consistent layout including title, actions, tags, and navigation options.

Import: `import { Card } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`title`** `string` **(required)** - The title of the component.
- **`subhead`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - The subheading for the component, which is optional.
- **`emphasizeTitle`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Adds visual emphasis to Card title
- **`actions`** `ActionItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Array of action items displayed in the card header (or merged with navigations at >=800px width). Actions represent operations on the card itself (edit, download, delete), in contrast to `navigations` which take the user elsewhere.

  ```ts
  actions={[
    { label: 'Edit', icon: Edit, onClick: () => editItem(id) },
    { label: 'Download', icon: Download, href: '/export' },
    { label: 'Delete', icon: TrashCan, onClick: () => remove(id), showLoading: true }
  ]}
  ```
- **`noPrimaryAction`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Removes visual emphasis from primary action.
- **`forceOverflow`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Forces the action set to overflow if there are too many actions.
- **`tags`** `TagItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Array of tags displayed in the tag area. By default tags sit in the header background; set `tagsInBody` to move them into the content area. Tags can be informational or interactive (via `onClick`).

  ```ts
  tags={[
    { label: 'In Progress', type: 'blue' },
    { label: 'High Priority', type: 'red', emphasize: true },
    { label: 'View team', type: 'gray', onClick: () => showTeam() }
  ]}
  ```
- **`tagsInBody`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Determines whether the tags should be displayed in the body of the card.
- **`navigations`** `NavigationItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Array of navigation items rendered as buttons at the bottom of the card, or merged into the header action area at >=800px width. Use navigations to send the user to related screens (cf. `actions`, which operate on the card itself). Items render in reverse order, so the first item appears rightmost and is styled as the primary action unless `noPrimaryNavigation` is set.

  ```ts
  navigations={[
    { label: 'View Details', href: '/items/42' },
    { label: 'Git Repository', href: 'https://github.com/...', icon: LogoGithub },
    { label: 'API Docs', href: '/docs', disabled: true }
  ]}
  ```
- **`noPrimaryNavigation`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Determines whether the primary navigation should not have visual emphasis.
- **`role`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - The ARIA role for the card. Defaults to "listitem" when within a CardGrid.
- **`image`** `CardImage | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Optional image for the card. Three sizing modes:  - **Locked** (`lockedAspect`): fixed aspect ratio, image crops to fit. Best for grids that    need uniform image proportions.  - **Unlocked with height**: fixed pixel height, flexible cropping. Best for grids that need    uniform card heights regardless of source image proportions.  - **Unlocked**: image fills available space. Best for hero-style single cards.

  ```ts
  // Locked square thumbnail
  image={{ src: '/photo.jpg', alt: 'Team photo', lockedAspect: 'square' }}
  
  // Fixed-height banner anchored to the top of the photo
  image={{ src: '/banner.jpg', alt: '', height: '180px', anchor: 'object-top' }}
  
  // Custom aspect ratio at the bottom of the card
  image={{ src: '/wide.jpg', alt: 'Sunset', lockedAspect: '21/9', position: 'bottom' }}
  ```
- **`headerLevel`** `number` (default: `3`) - HTML heading level (h1-h6) for the card title.

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Tab` | Moves focus between interactive elements |
| `Arrow Keys` | Navigate between card navigation items |
| `Enter/Space` | Activate focused action or navigation item |

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Card } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
  import { Add, Download } from 'carbon-icons-svelte'
</script>

<Card
  title="Project Overview"
  subhead="Current status"
  actions={[
    { label: 'Add Task', icon: Add },
    { label: 'Download', icon: Download }
  ]}
  tags={[
    { label: 'In Progress' },
    { label: 'High Priority' }
  ]}>
  <p>Sunlit orange groves stretched endlessly across rolling hills. Ripe citrus beneath California's golden afternoon sky.</p>
</Card>
```

### ColumnList

> A responsive data table component with support for expandable rows, actions, and column management.

Import: `import { ColumnList } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`columns`** `ColumnDefinition<T>[]` **(required)** - Array of column definitions that specify how to display each column in the table.
- **`rows`** `T[]` **(required)** - Array of data rows to be displayed in the table.
- **`title`** `string` **(required)** - A descriptive title for the list. Will be used as the aria-label for the list and to provide context in various places.
- **`responsiveColumns`** `((width: number) => string[]) | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Function to manually handle responsive column visibility based on table width. Given a width for the table, returns the list of column ids that should be displayed by default. The final column listed will be eligible to be replaced by another user-selected column.
- **`autoHideColumns`** `boolean | number | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Automatically hide columns when they don't fit. `responsiveColumns` will take precedence if both are provided. - `true` uses default min-width of 200px per column - number specifies custom average min-width in pixels
- **`expandable`** `boolean | ((row: T) => boolean)` - Controls row expansion behavior when default slot content is provided. Can be a boolean to enable/disable for all rows, or a function to specify per row.
- **`expanded`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Determines if default slot content is shown for all rows without requiring expansion.
- **`selectedActions`** `undefined | ((rows: T[]) => ActionItem[])` (default: `undefined`) - Function to generate action items for selected rows. When provided, checkboxes will be automatically rendered next to each row.
- **`noSelectAll`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Disables the select/deselect all functionality when using selectedActions.
- **`selectable`** `(row: T) => boolean` - Function to determine if a row should be selectable.
- **`actions`** `undefined | ((row: T) => ActionItem[])` (default: `undefined`) - Function to generate action items for each row. Actions will be placed in a column on the far right.
- **`actionsReverse`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Set this to true to reverse the order of the action buttons in each row. This will also put the overflow menu on the right side of the row. Order within the overflow menu will not be changed.
- **`listActions`** `ActionItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Array of action items to display at the top of the table. Best used for actions that affect the table's display rather than list manipulation.
- **`noItemsKind`** `'error' | 'info' | 'info-square' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'warning-alt'` (default: `'info'`) - Kind for search/filter active state (when filters or search are active but return no results).
- **`noItemsTitle`** `string` (default: `'No results found.'`) - Title for search/filter active state (when filters or search are active but return no results).
- **`noItemsSubtitle`** `string` (default: `'You may need to refine your searched terms, filters or try again.'`) - Subtitle for search/filter active state (when filters or search are active but return no results).
- **`dateFilterFields`** `string[]` (default: `[]`) - Field / path names that represent date/time filters. Used to show specialized empty message when date filters are active.
- **`emptyKind`** `'error' | 'info' | 'info-square' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'warning-alt'` (default: `'info'`) - Kind for true empty state (no filters, no search, no data).
- **`emptyTitle`** `string` (default: `'No entries found'`) - Title for true empty state (no filters, no search, no data).
- **`emptySubtitle`** `string` (default: empty string) - Subtitle for true empty state (no filters, no search, no data).
- **`dateFilterKind`** `'error' | 'info' | 'info-square' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'warning-alt'` (default: `'info'`) - Kind for date filter active state.
- **`dateFilterTitle`** `string` (default: `'No entries found.'`) - Title for date filter active state.
- **`dateFilterSubtitle`** `string` (default: `'Either no entries exist, or they fall outside the active time period.'`) - Subtitle for date filter active state.
- **`stickyHeader`** `boolean` (default: `true`) - By default the header row will stick to the top of the screen when scrolling. Set this to false to disable that behavior.
- **`searchable`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - If true, the list will be searchable. This will add a search input to the header.
- **`skipUrlState`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - If true, the filters will not update the URL state when changed.
- **`skipGoto`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - If true, the filter button will not navigate to a new URL when changed.
- **`urlKey`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - When set, namespaces all URL filter params under this key so that multiple ColumnLists on the same page can maintain independent URL state.
- **`filterTitle`** `string` (default: `'List Filters'`) - Title for the filter panel, if applicable.
- **`actionsMaxButtons`** `number` (default: `4`) - Maximum number of visible action buttons on each row - excess will overflow.
- **`actionsIncludeLabels`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - If true, the labels for action buttons will be shown when space allows.
- **`listActionsMaxButtons`** `number` (default: `4`) - Maximum number of visible action buttons for list actions (in the top right of the whole columnlist) before overflow.
- **`listActionsIncludeLabels`** `boolean` (default: `true`) - If true, the labels for list actions will be shown when space allows.
- **`selectedActionsMaxButtons`** `number` (default: `4`) - Maximum number of visible action buttons for selected actions (actions that may be taken on a set of selected rows) before overflow.
- **`selectedActionsIncludeLabels`** `boolean` (default: `true`) - If true, the labels for selected actions will be shown when space allows.
- **`expandOnPrint`** `boolean` (default: `true`) - If true, expandable rows will automatically expand when printing. Useful to make sure all content is captured when printing.

#### Slots

| Slot | Slot Props | Description |
|------|------------|-------------|
| default | `{ row: T }` | - |
| filters | `{ data: T }` | - |
| smallFilters | `{ data: T, quickslot: true }` | - |

#### Events

| Event | Type | Detail | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| on:filter | dispatched | - | - |
| on:search | dispatched | - | - |

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Space` | Toggle row selection |
| `Enter` | Activate row action or expansion |

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { ColumnList } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
  import type { ColumnDefinition } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'

  interface User {
    id: number
    name: string
    email: string
    role: string
  }
  // Providing an href for the email column will use OptionalLink to wrap the content in an anchor tag
  const columns: ColumnDefinition<User>[] = [
    { id: 'name', label: 'Name', get: 'name', class: 'name-class' },
    {
      id: 'email',
      label: 'Email',
      get: 'email',
      href: (row) => `mailto:${row.email}`,
      class: () => 'email-class'
    },
    { id: 'role', label: 'Role', get: 'role', fixed: '120px' }
  ]

  const users = [
    { id: 1, name: 'John Doe', email: 'john@example.com', role: 'Admin' },
    { id: 2, name: 'Jane Smith', email: 'jane@example.com', role: 'User' },
    { id: 3, name: 'Bob Wilson', email: 'bob@example.com', role: 'Editor' },
    { id: 4, name: 'Mark Markson', email: 'mark@example.com', role: 'AVP' },
    { id: 5, name: 'Boko Bobcat', email: 'boko@example.com', role: 'Mascot' },
    { id: 6, name: 'Tiffany Test', email: 'tiffany@example.com', role: 'Tester' }
  ]
</script>

<ColumnList
  title="Users"
  {columns}
  rows={users}
  stickyHeader
/>
```

### ErrorPage

> A full-page error display that renders user-friendly messages for common HTTP errors (400, 403, 404, 500). Place it in your root +error.svelte to automatically handle SvelteKit error responses.

#### Guidance

Place this component in your root `+error.svelte`. It automatically displays the correct error page based on the HTTP status code (400, 403, 404, 500).

Basic usage: import `ErrorPage` from `@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte` and place `<ErrorPage />` in your `+error.svelte` with no props. It reads from SvelteKit's `$page.status` and `$page.error` automatically.

The `error` prop accepts `{ status: number, message: string }`. Use this when handling errors in your root `+layout.svelte`: if your root `+layout.ts` can fail (e.g. network requests), catch the error there and return it as data instead of throwing, since `+error.svelte` renders inside the layout and can't display if the layout itself errors. Then in your root `+layout.svelte`, conditionally render `<ErrorPage error={data.error} />` when the error is present.

Import: `import { ErrorPage } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`error`** `{ status: number, message: string } | undefined` (default: `undefined`)

### FilterUI

> FilterUI is a flexible component that provides a powerful filtering interface for an application. It supports quick filters, main/dialog filters via the PanelFormDialog interface, tabs, and search functionality. The component can automatically handle URL state management and provides both immediate and deferred filter application modes. FieldHidden should be avoided within FilterUI as it will effect the filter count.

Import: `import { FilterUI } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`search`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Shows a search input field when true.
- **`searchDebounceMs`** `number` (default: `500`) - Milliseconds to wait after the user stops typing before triggering a search.
- **`searchQuickClass`** `string` (default: empty string) - A CSS class for the container around the search, but only when in the quick filters area. Use this to adjust the width of the search bar.
- **`quickFilterWidth`** `number` (default: `800`) - This is the viewport width in px under which the quick filters will be moved inside the panel with the rest of the filters. If you only have a search bar, or one quick filter, you can set this lower, or if you have a lot of quick filters, you can set this higher.
- **`noApply`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Set this true if you always expect filtering to be fast. It will send the 'apply' event every time the user interacts with the filters, instead of waiting for them to hit an Apply button.
- **`skipUrlState`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Default behavior is to save the state of the applied filters in the address bar so that the page can be bookmarked. Set this true if you don't want this behavior, e.g. you have two FilterUI instances on the screen at once.
- **`skipGoto`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Default behavior is to goto() the new URL when the filters are applied. This will re-run the load() function in your +page.ts, so that your table gets new data. In rare cases, your load function may be particularly heavy, like on a dashboard screen with many widgets. In those cases, you may set this true and you will only get the url in the address bar, but the load function will not re-run. You will have to listen for the 'apply' event and manually make API calls to freshen your data.  This prop has no effect if skipUrlState is true, because that skips both the goto() effect and the address bar update.
- **`tabs`** `TabRadioItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Array of tab objects with `{ label: string, value: string }` shape.
- **`tabsAriaLabel`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Accessible name for the tab radiogroup. Describes what the tabs select among (e.g. "View mode", "Filter by status"). Required for screen reader users when `tabs` is non-empty. Prefer `tabsAriaLabelledBy` if a visible heading already labels the tabs.
- **`tabsAriaLabelledBy`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - ID of an element that labels the tab radiogroup. Takes precedence over `tabsAriaLabel` when both are set.

#### Slots

| Slot | Slot Props | Description |
|------|------------|-------------|
| default | - | - |
| quickfilters | `{ quickslot: true }` | - |

#### Events

| Event | Type | Detail | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| on:apply | dispatched | - | Triggered when filters are applied, either through the Apply button or immediately if noApply is true. |
| on:mount | dispatched | - | Triggered when the component first mounts, providing initial filter state. |

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { FilterUI } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
  import { FieldMultiselect } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'

  let filterDataBasic: Record<string, any> | undefined

</script>

<FilterUI
  search
  skipUrlState={true}
  on:apply={(e) => { filterDataBasic = e.detail }}
  on:mount={(e) => { filterDataBasic = e.detail }}>
<FieldMultiselect
  path="status"
  label="Status"
  items={[
    { value: 'active', label: 'Active' },
    { value: 'inactive', label: 'Inactive' }
  ]}
/>
</FilterUI>

<p>Event Data</p>
<pre>{JSON.stringify(filterDataBasic, null, 2)}</pre>
```

  const tags: TagItem[] = [

    { label: 'In Progress', type: 'cyan' }
  ]
</script>

<IntroPanel
  title="Welcome to the Dashboard"

  {tags}
/>

### LinkSet

> A group of styled hyperlinks arranged in a set. Supports different sizes, alignment, states, and icons, and automatically handles external (outbound) links with the launch icon, new-tab behavior, and accessibility.

Import: `import { LinkSet } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`
Types: `import type { LinkItem } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`links`** `LinkItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Array of links included in the set.
- **`align`** `'left' | 'center' | 'right'` (default: `'center'`) - Horizontal alignment of the links within the set.
- **`size`** `'sm' | 'lg' | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Size of the links.
- **`describedById`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - ID of an element that describes this set of links (applied to each link as aria-describedby).
- **`stacked`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Stack links vertically instead of horizontally.

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { LinkSet } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
  import { ArrowRight } from 'carbon-icons-svelte'
  import type { LinkItem } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'

  // The external URL is auto-detected (cross-origin) and rendered as an outbound link: launch icon,
  // opens in a new tab, and security rel attributes. The relative URLs stay internal links.
  const links: LinkItem[] = [
    { label: 'External link', href: 'https://carbon-components-svelte.onrender.com/' },
    { label: 'Regular link', href: '/component/ActionSet' },
    { label: 'Regular link with icon', href: '/component/TagSet', icon: ArrowRight }
  ]
</script>

<LinkSet {links} />
```

### OptionalLink

> OptionalLink is a utility component that conditionally renders either an anchor tag or its children directly, based on whether an href prop is provided. Useful in data display contexts where some items may be clickable while others are not.

Import: `import { OptionalLink } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`href`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - If provided, the content will be wrapped in an anchor tag with this URL. If not provided, the content will be rendered directly without a wrapper.

#### Events

| Event | Type | Detail | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| on:click | forwarded | - | - |

This component forwards additional props to a via `$$restProps`.

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { OptionalLink } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
</script>

<OptionalLink href="https://www.txst.edu/">
  This will be a link
</OptionalLink>

<OptionalLink>
  This will be plain text
</OptionalLink>
```

### PageActions

> PageActions is a container component that handles positioning action buttons at the page level. Under the hood, it uses the ActionSet component with includeLabels set to true. It is designed to provide consistent placement and styling for primary and secondary page-level actions, distinguishing them from component-level actions found in panels, tables, cards, etc.

Import: `import { PageActions } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`actions`** `ActionItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Array of action items to display. Each action item can have
- **`noPrimaryAction`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - If true, all actions will be styled as secondary buttons instead of having the first action styled as primary.
- **`maxButtons`** `number` (default: `3`) - Maximum number of visible buttons before collapsing additional actions into an overflow menu.

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { PageActions } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
    import { Save, ArrowLeft, Document, DocumentBlank } from 'carbon-icons-svelte'

    const showConfirmation = (config: { key: string }) => {
      alert(`Showing confirmation for: ${config.key}`)
    }
  </script>

  <div class="flow [ p-4 bg-gray-100 ]">
    <h2 class="[ text-xl mb-4 ]">Edit Department Information</h2>

    <PageActions
        actions={[{ label: 'Start with entries', onClick: () => { showConfirmation({ key: 'initCopy' }) }, icon: Document }, { label: 'Start from scratch', onClick: () => { showConfirmation({ key: 'initScratch' }) }, icon: DocumentBlank }]}
        class="[ justify-start flex-grow ]"
    />

    <div class="[ mb-4 ]">
        <div class="[ bg-white p-4 rounded ]">
          <p class="[ text-gray-600 ]">Main page content</p>
        </div>
      </div>
  </div>
```

### Pagination

> A Pagination component that provides a user interface for navigating through paginated data. It supports customizable page sizes, URL state persistence, and works seamlessly with SvelteKit's routing system.

Import: `import { Pagination } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`page`** `number` (default: `1`) - Current page number, starting from 1. Used to control which page of results is displayed.
- **`totalItems`** `number | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Total number of items in the dataset. Used to calculate the total number of pages and display the item range text (e.g., "1-100 of 500 items").
- **`visibleItems`** `number | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Number of items currently visible. Only necessary if totalItems is not available. Used in cases where the total count might be unknown but the current page size is known.
- **`pageSize`** `25 | 100 | 500` (default: `100`) - Number of items to display per page. Only allows specific values to maintain consistent page sizes across the application.
- **`chooseSize`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Whether to allow users to change the page size via a dropdown menu. When false, the page size selector will be disabled.
- **`noun`** `string` (default: `'item'`) - Singular form of the item type being paginated (e.g., "user", "record", "item"). Used in the pagination text for better context.
- **`nounPlural`** `string` (default: `'items'`) - Plural form of the item type being paginated (e.g., "users", "records", "items"). Used in the pagination text when referring to multiple items.
- **`skipUrlState`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Default behavior is to save the state of the applied filters in the address bar so that the page can be bookmarked. Set this true if you don't want this behavior, e.g. you have two FilterUI instances on the screen at once.
- **`skipGoto`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Default behavior is to goto() the new URL when the filters are applied. This will re-run the load() function in your +page.ts, so that your table gets new data. In rare cases, your load function may be particularly heavy, like on a dashboard screen with many widgets. In those cases, you may set this true and you will only get the url in the address bar, but the load function will not re-run. You will have to listen for the 'apply' event and manually make API calls to freshen your data.  This prop has no effect if skipUrlState is true, because that skips both the goto() effect and the address bar update.
- **`contentSize`** `'small' | 'large'` (default: `'small'`) - The size of the content using pagination. This affects the available page sizes. Use 'small' for smaller content (e.g., table with rows) and 'large' for larger content (e.g., cards, images).

#### Events

| Event | Type | Detail | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| on:mount | dispatched | - | Fired when component mounts. |
| on:update | dispatched | - | Fired when page or page size changes. |

This component forwards additional props to the underlying component via `$$restProps`.

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Pagination } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'

  const page = 1
  const totalItems = 1063
</script>

<Pagination
  {page}
  {totalItems}
  noun="goose"
  nounPlural="geese"
/>
```

### Panel

> A Panel is an optionally collapsible container component that provides content organization with optional headers, tabs, and action buttons. It can be used to create hierarchical layouts with multiple levels of information. Header and body colors can be customized to match design needs.

Import: `import { Panel } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`title`** `string` **(required)** - The title displayed in the panel header.
- **`actions`** `ActionItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Array of actions to display in the panel header.
- **`noPrimaryAction`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - If true, no action will be highlighted via primary button styles.
- **`maxButtons`** `number` (default: `4`) - Maximum number of visible action buttons before overflow.
- **`forceOverflow`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Force all actions into overflow menu.
- **`hideActionsWhenCollapsed`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Hide actions when panel is collapsed.
- **`tabs`** `PanelTabs[]` (default: `[]`) - Configuration for tabbed content.
- **`tabsContainer`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Use container-style tabs
- **`selectedTab`** `number | undefined` - Index of the currently selected tab
- **`headerLevel`** `number` (default: `2`) - HTML heading level (h1-h6) for the panel title
- **`indentLevel`** `number` (default: `0`) - Number of indent levels for nested panels
- **`expandable`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Whether the panel can be collapsed/expanded
- **`expanded`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Whether an expandable panel is currently expanded
- **`backgroundColor`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Background color override for the panel content area
- **`headerBackgroundColor`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Background color override for the panel header
- **`headerTextColor`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Text color override for the panel header. Use to achieve appropriate contrast in combination with headerBackgroundColor.
- **`expandOnPrint`** `boolean` (default: `true`) - If true, expandable rows will automatically expand when printing. Useful to make sure all content is captured when printing.

#### Slots

| Slot | Slot Props | Description |
|------|------------|-------------|
| default | `{ tab: any }` | - |
| headerLeft | `{ tab: any; expanded: boolean }` | - |
| headerRight | `{ tab: any; expanded: boolean }` | - |

#### Events

| Event | Type | Detail | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| on:expand | dispatched | - | Fired when an expandable panel is expanded |

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Panel } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
  import { Edit, TrashCan } from 'carbon-icons-svelte'
</script>

<Panel title="Basic Panel">
  <p>This is the content of a basic panel.</p>
  <p>At its simplest, a Panel requires only a title and content.</p>
</Panel>

<Panel
title="Panel with Actions"
actions={[
  {
    label: 'Edit',
    icon: Edit,
    onClick: () => { alert('Edit clicked') }
  },
  {
    label: 'Delete',
    icon: TrashCan,
    disabled: true
  }
]}
>
  <p>Panel content with header actions.</p>
</Panel>
<Panel expandable expanded title="Panel" headerLevel={1} >
  <p>this panel is set to <code>h1</code></p>
</Panel>
<Panel expandable expanded title="Panel" headerLevel={2} >
  <p>this panel is set to <code>h2</code></p>
</Panel>
<Panel expandable expanded title="Panel" headerLevel={3} >
  <p>this panel is set to <code>h3</code></p>
</Panel>
<Panel expandable expanded title="Panel" headerLevel={4} >
  <p>this panel is set to <code>h4</code></p>
</Panel>
<Panel expandable expanded title="Panel" headerLevel={5} >
  <p>this panel is set to <code>h5</code></p>
</Panel>
<Panel expandable expanded title="Panel" headerLevel={6} >
  <p>this panel is set to <code>h6</code></p>
</Panel>
```

### TabRadio

> A component that combines tab-style navigation with radio button functionality for mutually exclusive selections.

Import: `import { TabRadio } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`tabs`** `TabRadioItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Array of tab items to be displayed. Each item can have a label, value, icon, and disabled state.
- **`selectedIndex`** `number` (default: `0`) - Zero-based index of the currently selected tab. Will be automatically constrained to valid values if out of bounds.
- **`value`** `any` (default: `undefined`) - Current value of the selected tab. Updated when selection changes.
- **`ariaLabel`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Accessible name for the radiogroup. Describes what the user is selecting among (e.g. "View mode", "Filter by status"). Announced by screen readers when focus enters the group. Prefer `ariaLabelledBy` if a visible heading already labels it.
- **`ariaLabelledBy`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - ID of an element that labels the radiogroup. Takes precedence over `ariaLabel` when both are set.

#### Events

| Event | Type | Detail | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| on:change | dispatched | `EventDetail` | [event description] |

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `← / ↑` | Move to previous tab |
| `→ / ↓` | Move to next tab |

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { TabRadio } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'

  let value = 'tab1'

  const tabs = [
    { label: 'Tab 1', value: 'tab1' },
    { label: 'Tab 2', value: 'tab2' },
    { label: 'Tab 3', value: 'tab3' }
  ]
</script>

<TabRadio {tabs} bind:value ariaLabel="Example tabs" />

<div class="mt-4">
  Selected value: {value}
</div>
```

### Toasts

> A toast notification system that displays temporary messages to the user.

Import: `import { Toasts } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`lowContrast`** `boolean` (default: `true`)

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { toasts } from '@txstate-mws/svelte-components'
    import { Button } from 'carbon-components-svelte'
    import { Toasts } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
</script>

<!--
Toast Interface from @txstate-mws/svelte-components

Properties:
- title?: string
- message: string
- type?: 'error' | 'warning' | 'info' | 'success' (default: 'error')
- ttlMs?: number (default: 8000ms for errors/warnings, 5000ms for success/info)

Special Values:
- ttlMs: Use Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER for permanent toasts
-->

<Toasts />
<Button
  on:click={() => toasts.add({
    type: 'success',
    title: 'Success',
    message: 'Your operation completed successfully. (permanent timing shown, e.g. use must dismiss manually)',
    ttlMs: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
  })}
>Success</Button>
<Button
  on:click={() => toasts.add({
    type: 'warning',
    title: 'Warning',
    message: 'Your operation has a warning, but was successful. (permanent timing shown, e.g. use must dismiss manually)',
    ttlMs: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
  })}
>Warning</Button>
<Button
  on:click={() => toasts.add({
    type: 'error',
    title: 'Error',
    message: 'Your operation failed. (3000ms TTL shown)',
    ttlMs: 3000
  })}
>Error</Button>
<Button
  on:click={() => toasts.add({
    type: 'info',
    title: 'Information',
    message: 'This action necessitates more information displayed for the user. (default timing shown)'
  })}
>Info</Button>
```

### UIShell

> The UIShell component provides the primary navigation and layout structure for your application. It includes a header with application branding, navigation menus, and optional user profile actions. The shell provides a consistent layout with a collapsible side navigation panel and a main content area.

Import: `import { UIShell } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`appName`** `string` **(required)** - The name of your application that appears in the header.
- **`navRoot`** `LayoutStructureNodeRoot<LayoutStructureNodeRoot<LayoutStructureNode>> | Record<string, never> | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - The navigation structure for your application. Omit (or pass an empty object) to render the shell without a hamburger menu and side navigation.
- **`companyName`** `string` (default: empty string) - Company or organization name that appears before the appName in the header.
- **`userProfile`** `UserProfile | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - User profile information that appears in right navigation menu
- **`profilelinks`** `ShellItem[]` (default: `[]`) - Array of navigation items for the user profile menu.
- **`stickyHeader`** `boolean` (default: `true`) - Whether the header should stick to the top when scrolling

- **`recordInteraction`** `((evt: InteractionEvent) => Promise<void>) | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Function to record user interactions for analytics. If you provide this (if you use our sveltekit-utils library, it should be an easy passthrough), this component library will call it to record certain user interactions like opening and closing modals.
- **`showSiteMap`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Whether to show the site map button in the header

- **`printLogo`** `string` (default: `TXST_LOGO`) - Logo image path for the print-only header. Defaults to the TXST logo.

- **`loadingBarLabel`** `string` (default: `'Loading...'`) - Text announced while the navigation loading bar is showing.

## carbon-svelte: form fields

Imported from `@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte`. Fields are useless outside a `Form` or `PanelFormDialog`
(or, in a prompt component, the form the framework wraps around you).

### Common field props

Every `Field*` component takes these, in addition to its own props:

- **`path`** `string` **(required)** - the form data path this field binds to.
- **`conditional`** `boolean` (default: `true`) - when false, svelte-forms drops this field's value
  from the submitted data. This is how a branch that is no longer shown stops contributing stale
  answers; see [Rules that apply to every file](#rules-that-apply-to-every-file).
- **`defaultValue`** varies (default: `undefined`) - initial value.
- **`id`** `string` (default: `randomid()`) - element id, auto-generated.

Most fields forward anything else to the underlying Carbon component via `$$restProps`.

### FieldCardCheckboxList

> A form field component that displays a grid of selectable cards for multiple selection.

Import: `import { FieldCardCheckboxList } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'`

#### Props

- **`items`** `CardSelectItem[] | undefined` **(required)** - Array of card options
- **`number`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Set to true to treat values as numbers instead of strings
- **`json`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Set to true to serialize/deserialize values as JSON strings
- **`notNull`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - Set to true to prevent null/undefined values (will default to empty array)
- **`legendText`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Text to display in the fieldset legend
- **`labelText`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Alias for `legendText`. Preferred if set.
- **`ariaLabelledBy`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - ID of an element that labels the field group. Using aria-labelledby will override the legend/labelText for screen readers.
- **`ariaDescribedBy`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - ID of an element that describes the field group. Use this for supplementary instructions or hints.
- **`required`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - When true, the field is marked as required in the UI. This is only for visual indication and does not affect validation. Validation is handled by the API that receives the data.
- **`disabled`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - When true, the entire field group is disabled.
- **`helperText`** `string | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Optional helper text to display below the legend
- **`cardSize`** `string` (default: `'20rem'`) - CSS size for the grid minimum item width (like CardGrid)
- **`gap`** `string` (default: `'16px'`) - Gap between cards in the grid
- **`serialize`** `((value: any) => string) | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Custom function to serialize individual item values for form submission. Each item value is serialized independently before being stored in the array.
- **`deserialize`** `((value: string) => any) | undefined` (default: `undefined`) - Custom function to deserialize individual item values from form data. Each item value is deserialized independently after being retrieved from the array.

#### Slots

| Slot | Slot Props | Description |
|------|------------|-------------|
| default | `{ item: any; selected: any; index: any }` | - |

#### Events

| Event | Type | Detail | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| on:blur | dispatched | - | - |
| on:focus | dispatched | - | - |
| on:update | dispatched | - | - |

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Form } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
  import { FieldCardCheckboxList } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'
  import type { CardSelectItem } from '@txstate-mws/carbon-svelte'

  // String values (default)
  const features: CardSelectItem[] = [
    {
      value: 'analytics',
      title: 'Analytics Dashboard',
      subhead: 'Track your metrics',
      tags: [
        { label: 'Popular', type: 'green' }
      ],
      selectionLabel: 'Add this feature'
    },
    {
      value: 'notifications',
      title: 'Push Notifications',
      subhead: 'Stay informed',
      tags: [
        { label: 'Recommended', type: 'blue' }
      ],
      selectionLabel: 'Add this feature'
    },
    {
      value: 'api',
      title: 'API Access',
      subhead: 'Integrate with your tools',
      tags: [
        { label: 'Developer', type: 'purple' }
      ],
      selectionLabel: 'Add this feature'
    },
    {
      value: 'support',
      title: 'Priority Support',
      subhead: '24/7 assistance',
      tags: [
        { label: 'Premium', type: 'magenta' }
      ],
      selectionLabel: 'Add this feature'
    },
    {
      value: 'legacy',
      title: 'Legacy Integration',
      subhead: 'Connect to older systems',
      tags: [
        { label: 'Deprecated', type: 'red' }
      ],
      selectionLabel: 'Add this feature',
      disabled: true
    }
  ]

  // Numeric values (use number prop)
  const quantities: CardSelectItem[] = [
    { value: 1, title: 'One Item', subhead: 'Single quantity' },
    { value: 5, title: 'Five Items', subhead: 'Small batch' },
    { value: 10, title: 'Ten Items', subhead: 'Medium batch' },
    { value: 25, title: 'Twenty-Five Items', subhead: 'Large batch' }
  ]

  // Object values (use json prop)
  const configs: CardSelectItem[] = [
    { value: { id: 1, type: 'basic', tier: 'free' }, title: 'Basic Config', subhead: 'Free tier' },
    { value: { id: 2, type: 'standard', tier: 'paid' }, title: 'Standard Config', subhead: 'Paid tier' },
    { value: { id: 3, type: 'premium', tier: 'enterprise' }, title: 'Premium Config', subhead: 'Enterprise tier' }
  ]
</script>

<Form let:data>
  <FieldCardCheckboxList
    path="selectedFeatures"
    legendText="Select Features for Your Plan"
    items={features}
  >
    <svelte:fragment slot="default" let:item>
      <p>
        {#if item.value === 'analytics'}
          Real-time data visualization and reporting
        {:else if item.value === 'notifications'}
          Email, SMS, and in-app notifications
        {:else if item.value === 'api'}
          RESTful API with full documentation
        {:else if item.value === 'support'}
          Dedicated support team available anytime
        {:else}
          Connect to legacy SOAP and XML systems
        {/if}
      </p>
    </svelte:fragment>
  </FieldCardCheckboxList>
  <div class="mt-6 p-4">Selected values (strings):</div>
  <pre class="mt-4">{JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)}</pre>
</Form>

<h3 class="mt-8 mb-4">With Numeric Values (number prop)</h3>
<Form let:data>
  <FieldCardCheckboxList
    path="quantities"
    legendText="Select Quantities"
    helperText="Values should be numbers, not strings"
    items={quantities}
    number
  />
  <div class="mt-6 p-4">Selected values (should be numbers like [1, 5] not ["1", "5"]):</div>
  <pre class="mt-4">{JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)}</pre>
</Form>

<h3 class="mt-8 mb-4">With Object Values (json prop)</h3>
<Form let:data>
  <FieldCardCheckboxList
    path="configs"
    legendText="Select Configurations"
    helperText="Values should be objects, not JSON strings"
    items={configs}
    json
  />
  <div class="mt-6 p-4">Selected values (should be objects like [{`{id:1,...}`}]):</div>
  <pre class="mt-4">{JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)}</pre>
</Form>
```

- **`disabled`** `boolean` (default: `false`) - When true, the entire field group is disabled.
